'''Stephen Lee''' ({{zh|c=李中漢|p=Lǐ Zhōnghàn}}; born 25 October 1955) is an American chemist. He is the son of [[Tsung-Dao Lee]], the winner of the 1957 [[Nobel Prize in Physics]]. He is currently a professor at [[Cornell University]].<ref name=homepage>{{cite web|url=https://chemistry.cornell.edu/faculty/detail.cfm?netid=sl137 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110807092244/http://chemistry.cornell.edu/faculty/detail.cfm?netid=sl137 |url-status=dead |archive-date=August 7, 2011 |title=Stephen Lee, Professor |accessdate=2013-09-25 |publisher=Cornell University}}</ref>

==Education==
Lee attended the [[International School of Geneva]], Switzerland and [[Yale University]], from which he graduated with a BA in 1978. He later received his PhD from the [[University of Chicago]] in 1985.

==Career==
In 1993, Lee received the [[MacArthur Award]] for his work in the field of physics and chemistry.{{citation needed|date=September 2013}} In addition, he has received an award from the [[Alfred P. Sloan Foundation]] for his continued research.

In 1999, Lee joined [[Cornell University]] as a professor of solid state chemistry in the chemistry and chemical biology department from the [[University of Michigan]], where he had been associate professor of chemistry since 1993.

He currently continues his teaching career at Cornell, where he instructs students in (honors) general chemistry and introduction to chemistry courses. During the past 10 years,{{clarify|date=September 2013}} Lee has devoted his summer to helping incoming freshmen learn basic chemistry to prepare them for the academic year. This has been considered part of Lee's philanthropic work, as he teaches these summer courses [[probono]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-05-16 |title='I've learned what it means to be a conscientious scientist' {{!}} Department of Chemistry and Chemical Biology |url=https://chemistry.cornell.edu/news/ive-learned-what-it-means-be-conscientious-scientist |access-date=2026-01-08 |website=chemistry.cornell.edu |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Hovis |first={{!}} Kathy |last2=A |last3=Communications |first3=S. |date=2020-07-10 |title=Chemistry students offer summer session for peers |url=https://as.cornell.edu/news/chemistry-students-offer-summer-session-peers |access-date=2026-01-08 |website=as.cornell.edu |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2019-05-10 |title=Hendryck Gellineau: ‘Organic Chemistry is essentially abstract art with a side of involved logic’ {{!}} Department of Chemistry and Chemical Biology |url=https://chemistry.cornell.edu/news/hendryck-gellineau-organic-chemistry-essentially-abstract-art-side-involved-logic |access-date=2026-01-08 |website=chemistry.cornell.edu |language=en}}</ref>

His current research involves developing stronger porous solids in which all the host porous bonds are covalent in character. Lee is also researching ways to introduce cross-linkable guests (such as di-isocyanides or disilyltriflates) which will react with nucleophilic groups, leading to a fully covalent organic porous solid. He also hopes to develop a long range order in intermetallic phases: Examine noble metal alloys where unit cell dimensions range from just a few, to almost 104 Å.<ref name=homepage/>

==Personal life==
Stephen Lee was born to 1957 Nobel Prize winner in Physics [[Tsung-Dao Lee]] and Hui-Chun Jeannette Chin ({{zh|c=秦惠莙|p=Qín Huìjūn}}), who died in 1996. Lee has one brother, James Lee ({{zh |c = 李中清 |p = Lǐ Zhōngqīng}}; born 1952), who is the dean of the School of Humanities and Social Science at the [[Hong Kong University of Science and Technology]] and chair professor of the Division of Social Science at the same university.
